due_when.clears_when: A CI guard fails when a module under src/ writes a runtime_logs/*_state.json or *_alerts.jsonl path that has no _LOG_FILES entry, unless the writer carries an explicit `# read-surface: none - <reason>` marker. THREE REQUIREMENTS, each from a mistake this repo has already made and none of them optional: (1) THE MARKER MUST BE VERIFIED, NOT PRESENCE-ONLY — it must name something checkable, because new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only `# data-wiring:` marker made the cheapest way to silence a real finding be to name a table that does not exist, and a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard. (2) IT MUST SHIP WITH A SELF-TEST PROVING IT FAILS on a planted writer with no allowlist entry — a guard whose failure path has never executed is a deploy, not a check. (3) IT MUST STATE ITS DENOMINATOR: how many writer sites it scanned, so a guard that silently stops matching (a renamed path helper, a new write idiom) reads as a shrinking population rather than as continued green. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: adding another name to _LOG_FILES. That is what was done all five times, and it is why there were five. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: extending the allowlist-vs-CLAUDE.md coherence test, which by construction cannot see an unlisted writer.
